title: TPL tooling config
description: Reference data consumed by tpl:* commands. Looked up as tpl.config.json at the directory where the commands are invoked, or passed explicitly via --config (so a shared file such as adr.config.json can be reused).

idFormat.description: TPL id / filename convention. `date-sequence` expects `TPL-YYYYMMDD-NN-<slug>.md` (id `TPL-YYYYMMDD-NN`); `issue-number` expects `TPL-<n>-<slug>.md` (id `TPL-<n>`, no zero padding).

topics.description: Controlled vocabulary for a TPL's `topic` field. Empty or omitted disables topic validation.

indexFile.description: Generated index file, relative to the TPL directory and inside it, with `/` separators (no backslash, no leading or trailing `/`, no `..`), and not named `TPL-*.md` directly in it, which would be read as a TPL (e.g. `index.md`). When set, `tpl regenerate` writes it, grouped by topic, and `tpl validate` checks it instead of README.md. Omit to keep a hand-maintained README index.

indexCheck.description: `false` turns off every index check in `tpl validate`: neither `indexFile` nor README.md is read, so a missing or out-of-date index is not a finding. For a repo whose index is written outside its PRs (e.g. by a scheduled regeneration PR), where the index may lag or not exist yet. `tpl regenerate` ignores it.

checklistHeading.description: Heading text of the checklist section, without `#` (e.g. `Checklist`). When set, each checklist item may end with `[guard: `path`]` (enforced by the named file) or `[judgment]` (not decidable by a program); `tpl validate` requires the section, at least one item, and well-formed markers, and needs source prefixes (`sourcePrefixes` or `--source-prefix`) to check guard paths; `tpl regenerate`, `tpl related --status`, `tpl checklist` and `tpl review-body` show the enforcement status derived from the markers. Omit to turn all of this off.

sourcePrefixes.description: Top-level directories that hold source (e.g. `packages`, `scripts`, `.github`). A code span in a TPL body counts as a source path only when its first segment is one of these: `tpl validate` checks that the path exists, and `tpl related --changed-files` / `--base` recall the TPL when that file changes. `--source-prefix` on the command line replaces this list. Omit to read no path from the body.

testFileInfixes.description: What a test file's name adds just before its extension (`foo.test.ts` → `foo.ts`; `_test` maps `foo_test.go` → `foo.go`). A TPL whose body names a test file is also recalled by `tpl related --changed-files` / `--base` when that source changes. An empty list turns the mapping off.
